column1: # ---- 03-contracts/C3 and C4 ----
C3 carries the ExecutionIntent payload at version 1.0 from L3 to L4.
Execution is the pre-existing market simulator, treated as an external system.
C3 is deliberately thin and carries intent only.
The C3 envelope adds planId, the gate the submission targets, an optional supersedes naming the previous planId whose open orders it replaces, and the degradation mode.
The degradation mode is echoed on C3 so Execution can refuse speculative flow in SAFE.
An order intent carries one row per order with a stable intentId that survives replaces.
The market field is one of Da, IdContinuous, IdAuction, AfrrCapacity or AfrrEnergy.
productId comes from the market calendar.
The side field is in the market frame, where sell means discharge.
limitPrice is tick-aligned and already rounded per the C0 rounding rule.
volume is lot-aligned and strictly positive.
validity is one of Ioc, Fok, GtdUntil(SlotId) or GtcUntilGate.
An order intent's tag is one of Arbitrage, PeakShave, ReserveHedge, Rebalance or CommitmentCover.
shadowValue is the Planner's indifference price, carried for audit only, and Execution must ignore it.
urgency is carried for audit only.

shadowValue and urgency cross the seam for settlement attribution rather than for execution, letting L5 answer whether the quoting policy traded through indifference without a private side channel between the Planner and the quoting policy.
Execution does not read shadowValue or urgency, enforced by the adapter interface exposing a projection that omits them.
DA requires a monotone schedule rather than a point order.
A DA bid curve carries price-ordered curvePoints and its slot.
DA curve monotonicity is asserted rather than declared.
Quantity must be non-increasing in price for a buy curve and non-decreasing for a sell curve.

A non-monotone DA curve indicates a Planner formulation error, most often a missing coupling constraint, and is a HALT because such a curve is both rejected by the exchange and diagnostic of a deeper problem.
The dispatch setpoint interface is fixed at C3 even though the physical controller is downstream of the Planner and out of scope.
pSetpoint is in the battery frame over the near horizon H_near.
socCorridorLower and socCorridorUpper are the band the controller must stay in to keep commitments feasible.
reserveObligationUp and reserveObligationDn are the confirmed awards the controller must be able to serve.
H_near is short, typically the next few slots.
The corridor rather than the setpoint is the binding instruction: the controller may deviate from the setpoint to follow an activation signal but never out of the corridor.
Every intent is physically deliverable given SOC, power and POI limits under the planned trajectory, and violation is a HALT.
Confirmed commitments in L0 are covered by the plan, and violation is a HALT.
No two intents exist for the same product and slot on the same side without a replacesIntentId chain, and violation is a HALT.
Prices are tick-aligned and volumes lot-aligned, and violation is a HALT.
In SAFE mode only CommitmentCover and cancel intents are present, and violation is a HALT.
Total planned discharge over any window respects energy availability including the reserve corridor, and violation is a HALT.
No sell intent is priced below shadowValue and no buy intent above it, and violation warns and blocks the intent.

The shadow-value price guard is a warning rather than a halt because covering a commitment at a loss is sometimes correct, but such intents must carry the CommitmentCover tag and an untagged violation is blocked.
No reason for an order crosses C3: Execution is strategy-independent and the tag is for settlement attribution only, not routing.
No Belief, valuation or scenario data crosses C3.
No expectation about fills crosses C3: the Planner's fill beliefs stay upstream and C3 is an instruction, not a forecast.
C4 carries the ExecutionOutcome payload at version 1.0 from L4 to L5.
Settlement can reconstruct the truth from the C4 payload plus metered reality alone, having no access to what the Planner intended, so ex-post accounting cannot be contaminated by ex-ante belief.
The C4 envelope adds settlementPeriod, isFinal versus provisional, and revisionOf for restatements, because meter data and imbalance prices arrive late and get corrected.
Provisional and final settlement data are both first-class.
The engine cannot wait for final data to keep operating and must not treat provisional data as final.
Every settlement artefact declares whether it is provisional or final, and a restatement is a new artefact referencing the old one, never an in-place edit.
intentId on a fill links back to C3 and is the only backward reference permitted, and it is an identifier rather than data.
A fill carries the executed price and the executed volume.
Fees are explicit on a fill and never netted into the price.
An unfilled order carries a disposition of Expired, Cancelled, Rejected or PartiallyFilled, a rejectReason populated for Rejected, and the residual volume that did not trade.
Unfilled orders are as important as fills, because without them the four-bucket error decomposition cannot separate being wrong about value from being unable to get the trade.
awardedUp and awardedDn are per block and are the binding obligation.
clearingPriceUp and clearingPriceDn are per block in EUR/MW/h.
activatedEnergyUp and activatedEnergyDn are realised per slot in kWh, with activation prices per slot in EUR/MWh.
deliveryShortfall is per slot, and a non-zero value triggers the reserve delivery invariant.
meteredPoiImport and meteredPoiExport are the billing-relevant series.
meteredLoad and meteredPv are sub-metered where available.
batteryChargeEnergy and batteryDischargeEnergy are measured at the battery terminal.
socMeasured is the end-of-slot state of charge.
Provisional meter data is routine.
imbalanceVolume is signed per slot, and the imbalance price is often final only weeks later.
Every fillId references an intentId submitted in this run, and violation is a HALT for a phantom fill.
Filled volume is at most the intended volume per intent across all fills, and violation is a HALT.
The energy balance poiImport − poiExport = load − pv + chargeEnergy − dischargeEnergy holds within meter tolerance, warning if provisional and halting if final.
deliveryShortfall equals zero, and violation alerts and halts because a reserve delivery failure is a prequalification risk.
socMeasured is consistent with charge and discharge energy and η within tolerance, and violation warns because drift indicates an η or SOH model error.
Every reserve award has a corresponding entry in the commitment ledger by end of tick, and violation is a HALT.
Persistent divergence between modelled and measured SOC is the earliest available signal that the efficiency or degradation model has drifted, and it is cheap to monitor.
The SOC consistency check feeds the model-error bucket in L5.
No Planner reasoning crosses C4; only intentId as an opaque key.
No Valuation output crosses C4.
No belief or forecast crosses C4, because Settlement recomputes truth from realised data and if it needed a forecast it would be doing valuation rather than settlement.
